reading: GRÜN · §86 — the replaced PG-14 solve: convergence to a half-device-pixel tolerance, and containment of all three labels
scope: arithmetic on committed constants, the committed layout spec and layout-golden-vectors-v1.1.json. No render, no server, no build, no browser.

subject.tolerance: half grows by < 0.5·k, k taken at the NEW half

whatThisRouteCannotSee: glyph advance is modelled as chars × em, so this route is BLIND to real glyph metrics by construction — which is why PINK's browser route found the second defect and this one could not. What it sees instead is the whole envelope: every layout, every width, every name length, including lengths no fixture contains.
collarMoreNotExercised: the vectors are L0 populations, so collarMore is null throughout. Its asymmetric right-hand reservation is in the solve and is NOT exercised here; §84 found the label renders zero times on the one served population, so it has no carrier anywhere yet.

findings.exactResidualNote: a non-zero residual is expected: the solve stops inside half a device pixel, so 'not contained exactly' counts the tolerance rather than a defect.

finding:
NO HOLE: in all 440 swept cases, every residual of half a device pixel or more occurs ONLY where the solve reached its 12-pass cap and therefore emitted data-frame-converged="false". There is no case that claims convergence and fails to contain.
§64's DEFECT IS CLOSED ACROSS THE ENVELOPE THAT EXPOSED IT. At a 16-character name at 420 px — where the old fixed-two-pass solve clipped by 1.59 px on 4 of 11 layouts — the worst residual is now 0.1068 px, and across every realistic name length (<= 32 characters) the worst anywhere is 0.2557 px, all below the half-pixel tolerance. The measure is counted at its real length (12 characters for a checked rank-1 body), which is the label §69 found wider than the title on four of five bodies.
136 of 440 cases reach the cap, all at names of 48/64/96/128 characters — not role names. The ascent there does not contract, which §64 established, so no finite pass count would contain them; what changed is that the product now SAYS so instead of emitting a frame that silently does not hold.
